newsitem.title: UK: UK's Whittard raises coffee prices by up to 14 pct.
newsitem.headline: UK's Whittard raises coffee prices by up to 14 pct.

text.p: Upmarket British coffee and tea retailer Whittard of Chelsea said on Friday it has raised coffee prices by up to 14 percent with immediate effect in response to the sharp increase in arabica bean costs.
Whittard said it had seen the price of green coffee risen by over 30 percent since January. It said the new retail price increase had not hit its coffee sales.
Whittard said a combination of human and natural disasters had contributed to the general world shortage of coffee thus forcing the prices up.
Civil war in Central Africa, general strikes in Colombia and leaf and berry disease destroying crops in South American and Indonesia were cited as the main factors, it said.
Whittard sells only pure origin arabica coffee.
"We have therefore had to reluctantly pass on part of the price increases to the customer with a maximum of 14 percent increase," a Whittard statement said.
Nestle UK and several leading supermarket chains including Tesco Plc have also raised shelf prices to reflect the steep rise in arabica bean costs.
Gala Coffee and Tea Ltd, which lifted its prices in March, has told its customers that another round of increase would take place from the end of May. -- Jalil Hamid, London newsroom +44 171 542 4985
